name: Apache ZooKeeper
summary: A replicated coordination service that presents a hierarchical namespace, session-scoped ephemeral state, ordered updates, and watches for distributed applications.

features.name: Hierarchical znode namespace
features.description: ZooKeeper exposes a slash-separated hierarchical namespace of znodes. Each znode can contain data, children, metadata, and an ACL, making coordination state addressable as a tree rather than as an unstructured key set.
benefits: Groups related coordination state under explicit paths
Supports small configuration, status, rendezvous, and ownership records
Makes namespace and access boundaries visible to clients
costs: The service is intended for relatively small coordination data rather than bulk objects
Path layout and ACL choices become part of the application contract
Tree operations can create contention around heavily shared parents

features.name: Session-scoped ephemeral state
features.description: A client session is maintained by the ZooKeeper cluster and can expire after the negotiated timeout. Ephemeral znodes owned by an expired session are deleted, enabling presence and ownership records tied to client liveness.
benefits: Represents process or service presence without a separate cleanup protocol
Supports locks, leader records, and service-discovery recipes
Makes session expiration an explicit failure transition
costs: Network partitions and timeout selection affect when ownership is withdrawn
Clients must distinguish temporary disconnection from session expiration
Ephemeral nodes cannot themselves have children

features.name: Ordered atomic coordination updates
features.description: ZooKeeper applies znode data access atomically and assigns each state change a zxid that exposes the service order of changes. Version checks can reject an update based on stale znode metadata.
benefits: Provides a coordination order for distributed state changes
Supports compare-and-update patterns with znode versions
Lets clients reason about updates without exposing replica internals
costs: The ordering scope is the ZooKeeper service, not an application-wide transaction across external systems
Version conflicts require retry or conflict handling
Quorum coordination adds latency and limits write availability during insufficient quorum

features.name: Watch-driven change notification
features.description: Clients may register watches through reads of znode data or children. Standard watches are one-time triggers, are ordered with replies and other events, and require the client to establish a new watch for future changes.
benefits: Avoids polling for many coordination changes
Preserves an observable order between a watch event and the corresponding new data
Supports event-driven configuration, membership, and lock recipes
costs: A standard watch does not report every intermediate change during a re-registration gap
Disconnected clients do not receive watch events until reconnection
Applications still need a read-and-reconcile step after notification

mathematical_views.question: How do path-addressed state, session ownership, and expiry produce a coordination state machine?
assumptions: The namespace is modeled as a rooted tree whose nodes carry data, metadata, and ACL state
A session is a liveness state with connected, disconnected, and expired transitions
Ephemeral-node deletion is modeled as a transition caused by session expiry, not by arbitrary client cleanup
The view abstracts network timing and does not claim a bound on failure-detection latency

mathematical_views.question: Which observations can a client derive from ordered znode updates and one-time watches?
assumptions: Each committed update has a service order represented by zxid
A standard watch is a pending notification that is removed after triggering
Clients re-read state after notification and do not infer unseen intermediate values
The model treats quorum replication as the source of committed service order

benefits: Explicit path-scoped coordination state and ACL boundaries
costs: Small-data limits and path/parent contention constrain modeling choices
Timeout and partition behavior can delay or prematurely change ownership

benefits: Service-wide update order and stale-write detection
costs: Quorum coordination adds write latency and availability dependencies
One-time watches can miss intermediate states and require reconciliation
